help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: Why the choices change: a source that fails definitively, a service that is turned off, unavailable, out of quota or not included in your plan, or a download already finished drop out of the lists or are shown as unavailable. Switching back and forth does not, by itself, eliminate any choice.

Progress: when choosing a source would mean losing the progress already reached, DebridPulse first asks Discard downloaded progress?. A service change that would mean losing progress is instead refused, with the reason would discard already downloaded data; change its source to confirm.

While a download is paused: choosing another source for a file that had already started downloading is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The service and source shown remain the current ones and, next to the service name, a message indicates where the file will go, for example Switches to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume. A new choice replaces it; choosing the source already in use removes it. After resuming the message becomes Switching to … until the change takes effect, then disappears. If a download's paused files were to go to different places, or the destination is not known, no destination is shown. A file never started has nothing to switch, so the new source simply applies when it starts. Choosing a service during the pause works as described above, except that the download stays paused: a service that can take over the link in use takes over immediately (the badge shows it), while one that must first prepare a copy shows Preparing … and takes over only after resuming. These messages appear in the rows of Download activity and Downloads; both kinds can appear at the same time.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb.backTranslation: Each debrid service has a Prepare backup torrents switch. It is on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox, whose torrent limits are more restrictive. When it is on, that service also adds the torrents that another service is delivering, so as to be ready to take over if needed; also, when you move a download to another service, the torrent already started is kept as a backup instead of being removed. This uses that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes precedence and reclaims it. Turn it off to reserve that service's slots for its own downloads: its backups are then removed. A choice already saved is kept.

help.howitworks.adding_same_thing.if_add.backTranslation: If you add a magnet, a {file_type} file, NZB or Metalink that DebridPulse is already working on (including one that failed and has not yet been removed), Already queued is shown and the existing download is kept instead of starting a second one. Web links are always added as a new download. Once a download has finished, been cancelled or been removed, adding the same source again starts a new download. When two downloads turn out to be downloading the same content, DebridPulse can merge them; the merged one shows Consolidated. When DebridPulse cannot prove that they match, the merged one instead shows Consolidated · Unverified. Merging does not change who requested the download: each account's request remains its own.

help.settings.downloads.download_behavio.backTranslation: Download behavior and limits: Download folder (with Browse) and Maximum simultaneous downloads. In Advanced settings: Material checkpoint interval and Controlled shutdown timeout (best not changed), Local network connections (off by default) to allow downloads from devices on your own private network, and Skip local connection confirmation so as not to ask every time. Even when allowed, DebridPulse never connects to the computer it is running on or to other non-private local addresses. Also here: Provider polling interval (how often a service is queried about the progress of the work it is preparing), Full synchronization interval (how often downloads are reconciled with every active premium account that lists its transfers; 0 turns it off) and Retries after resolution errors with Delay between retries (minutes) (how many times and after how long a failed resolution is retried, for any service, including Network sources).

A ZIP archive is extracted only without a password; these passwords are not tried for ZIP files. Each row contains one password, which is saved when you leave the row. Show all makes them visible; Clear passwords clears the whole list.

help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts lists every person with their role, how they sign in and whether the account is active. Click an account's name to see its details and activity, where a pending request can be withdrawn individually. Deactivate and Remove first show how many pending download requests the account has; those requests are withdrawn, a transfer also requested by someone else continues and completed downloads are never touched. Deactivation also ends the account's sign-ins and blocks its tokens; removal keeps the account's history and deletes its notification settings. A removed OIDC sign-in that comes back receives a new account, which stays deactivated until it is activated. Merge combines two or more accounts into the one you choose to keep; two accounts that share a verified email are flagged, but only “Merge” combines them.
